newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil ends firmer, off highs, heat supports.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil ends firmer, off highs, heat supports.

text.p: IPE gas oil futures closed firmer on Tuesday, but off the session high as NYMEX heating oil trimmed earlier gains.
The May contract settled $1.00 up at $166.50 a tonne, off the day's high of $167.75 a tonne.
"We had some good interest over here and the heat was strong," said one broker.
Dealers said unseasonably cool weather on both sides of the Atlantic was helping to boost demand for heating.
Weekly U.S. stocks data from the American Petroleum Institute (API), due to be released after the close of business on Tuesday, were expected to show tighter heating oil supplies.
Preliminary expectations from analysts forecast a draw of up to one million barrels on the previous week's levels.

Independent weather forecasters Weather Services Corp said on Tuesday that temperatures in the U.S. Northeast could be as much as 10-15 degrees Fahrenheit below normal in some of the major cities by Wednesday and Thursday. The U.K. and France saw temperatures turn significantly lower, it added.
June Brent was trading 10 cents up at $18.07 a barrel at 1720 GMT, having touched a session high of $18.19.
